records.product: Elvital ÖL Magique Veredelndes Haaröl (retailer listing name: "Elvital Öl Magique Haaröl")
records.g0_rationale: The frozen INCI declares NO Aqua anywhere in its 21 ingredients. ISODODECANE (r1, a volatile hydrocarbon carrier) leads, followed by DIMETHICONE r2 and DIMETHICONOL r3 (persistent silicones) and a lipid load — COCOS NUCIFERA OIL r4, SCLEROCARYA BIRREA (Marula) SEED OIL r8, CAMELLIA JAPONICA SEED OIL r9, CAPRYLIC/CAPRIC TRIGLYCERIDE r12. §3.1.2's decision order therefore stops at its first row, `anhydrous_serum_or_oil`, which is the §2.3 `excluded_anhydrous` condition verbatim ('No Aqua, or Aqua absent from the top of the list; cyclomethicone/dimethicone/oils lead → oil/serum category', SR §A.1), and §2.2's boundary table excludes 'Pure oils and anhydrous silicone serums → route to the oil/serum category'. The decision is made by architecture and function, never by the name 'Haaröl' (§2.3): the name is corroboration, and the same exclusion would follow for a product called a serum or a mist. The §2.4 rule-2 rinse test does NOT produce the exclusion here: block 4 of the manufacturer's own 10-block Anwendung („Als Intensivpflege vor der Haarwäsche … 10 Minuten vor der Haarwäsche verwenden") is a pre-wash step while blocks 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 are explicit leave-on uses — a genuinely dual-use direction, which under §2.4 rule 2 clause 2 keeps a record in-category for the rinse test and routes it to review (`dual_use_directions`). The operative exclusion is the anhydrous architecture, not the rinse test.

(2) Standing §14 identity trigger: the ONLY INCI capture for this product is a Müller.de retailer SKU ('Elvital Öl Magique Haaröl') whose identity to the manufacturer's full-name 'Veredelndes Haaröl' is inferred from matching pack size and matching Marula/Camellia composition, not confirmed by a shared GTIN or an exact name match — and Müller.de's own catalogue lists several similarly named 100 ml Öl Magique variants. assumption_notes: CLAIM-AUTHORITY DETERMINATION — the consequential call on this record (§2.4.1 rule 7, T14). The three loveamika.com claims are NOT admitted as `C2_cross_market_verified`; they remain C5 and creates_claim FALSE. Rule 7 requires BOTH prongs. Prong (b) is satisfied — sephora.de, a German-market C3/C4 retailer, corroborates the heat claim („Wärmeschutzwirkung bis 230 °C") and the UV claim („UV-Schutz"). Prong (a), IDENTITY VERIFICATION, FAILS: rule 7(a) requires the German-sold unit's formula fingerprint to be IDENTICAL to the claimed product's own published INCI on a set-for-set diff, order noise aside, OR a shared GTIN confirmed at a German retailer. No GTIN is confirmed by any source. And the two INCI captures are not identical set-for-set: the German-market sephora.de list carries THREE ingredients the manufacturer's list does not (Hexamethylindanopyran, Tetramethyl Acetyloctahydronaphthalenes, Vanillin). That is a set difference, not order noise. A plausible explanation exists — all three are fragrance/aroma chemicals of the kind EU labelling requires to be declared and US labelling does not — but rule 7 demands VERIFIED identity, and the rule's own guarding counter-example (Cantu) is explicit that a foreign claim may not be laundered onto a formula that is not SHOWN to be the same. §1.1 decides the direction: admitting the claim would set `provides_heat_protection: true` — an upgrade toward a more favourable value on unverified identity — while declining it holds the conservative value and routes to a human. Rule 3 therefore stands unchanged: the non-German page is C5, no amount of retailer corroboration substitutes for identity, and the heat binary is FALSE with `claim_authority_gap` routed. The four sephora.de claims are C3/C4 and creates_claim FALSE independently (§2.4.1 rule 1).

CONSEQUENCES of that determination, stated plainly so a reviewer can see what turns on it: `provides_heat_protection` is `false` (a `true` would follow immediately from admitting the claim, per §13.3 rule 1), the HEAT trace state is `not_claimed` rather than `claim_only`, the `heat_styling` focus is unavailable even though `application_stage` includes `pre_heat` with its verbatim direction sentence, and no „… ist ausgelobt" string is emitted. This is the designed conservative outcome of G13, and it is the single field a human reviewer should look at first on this record.

focus.primary = `smoothing`: §10.2 step 1 collects qualifying routes — `smoothing` qualifies (see smoothing_route); `heat_styling` fails its first conjunct (`provides_heat_protection` must be true); `detangling` fails both limbs (no C1/C2 positioning of any kind exists for this product, and the slip-dominant limb needs COND ≤ `moderate` with WT `low`); `volume_lightness` fails (WT not `low`, persistent film present); `curl_definition` fails at HOLD and at its negative gate; `repair` is unavailable (R2 `none_visible`); `shine` is not added because it would restate the smoothing film (§8.1, G3). Step 3 rank order makes the single qualifying route primary. NOTE on the anti-frizz user need: T9 removed HUM entirely and this product's entire identity is an anti-humidity claim — the `smoothing` focus is where that need lands, and it lands there WITHOUT asserting humidity performance, exactly as §7.9's removal rationale intends.

§10.2.1 recording requirement — observations that established COND: the LGN pair {Cetearyl Alcohol r6, Behentrimonium Chloride r9, Cetrimonium Chloride r10} together with the further lubrication route {Hippophae Rhamnoides oil r5}. The additional observation the smoothing route rests on: PHENYL TRIMETHICONE r12, the persistent-silicone film, which COND did not need to reach `high`. Under T13b's permissive reading a single admissible COND-establishing set suffices, and this reading is admissible on its own terms.
texture_fit row 3 applies: `weight_potential` is `high` and the absorbed slip observation names two or more independent M1 contributors present as architecture.

damage_fit row 2 applies: `conditioning_level` is `high` but there is no qualifying specialist route for row 3a — the only L6-adjacent species are two plain hydrolysates, and the cationic polymers that might have formed a film route sit below the marker and are not present as architecture. Row 3b is not reached (R2 `none_visible`).

IDENTITY DISCREPANCY recorded and not reconciled: sephora.de's 'Zusammensetzung' tab names „Polyquaternum-59" [sic] as a key UV-protective ingredient, but no Polyquaternium-59 or near variant appears in EITHER INCI capture — both declare Polyquaternium-11. This is recorded verbatim, it set no value, and it is carried to review. It is worth a reviewer's attention because Polyquaternium-55 (a different number again) IS a closed-list L9 heat member, and a mis-transcribed polymer number is exactly the kind of error that would move a heat state if it were ever read as evidence.

No counter-signal, confidence value or reading convention reached any projected field (G14, §10.1.1). In particular the §3.1.1 clause-3 below-marker note did not modify `persistence`, which projects `moderate` exactly as its rank-supported class says.

review_routing.notes: (1) `claim_authority_gap` (§2.4.1 rule 1, §13.3 rule 1) — the heat-protection claim exists only in German retailer copy and on a non-German manufacturer page that fails rule 7(a). The binary is `false` and the review decides whether a German-market manufacturer source exists and was simply not found, or whether the three-ingredient INCI delta is a pure EU-versus-US fragrance-labelling artifact that would satisfy rule 7(a) on a re-freeze. This is the highest-value review item on the record. (2) T17 `l9_member_without_claim` — Hydrolyzed Wheat Protein r8 sits above the marker with no claim-creating heat source; the mirror of trigger (1), and both point at the same decision. (3) §3.1.1 clause 3 below-marker routing — Polyquaternium-11 r18 and Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride r19 would qualify `permanent_cationic` but sit below the marker at r16, so PERS takes its rank-supported `neutral_non_volatile` and a human, not a rank heuristic whose variance is an open gap (§17.14, §17.18), decides whether this product's persistence and buildup profile is being under-stated (FS-20). (4) Standing §14 trigger 'a formula-source or identity conflict': the two INCI captures differ by three fragrance/aroma chemicals; no GTIN is confirmed by any source; the manufacturer states 450 °F while the German retailer states 230 °C; and sephora.de's composition tab names a polymer („Polyquaternum-59") that appears in neither ingredient list. (5) `tail_marker_dependence` — Ethylhexylglycerin r16 of 32 decided the 'present as architecture' read for Ceresin, Polyquaternium-11 and Guar HPTC, and therefore decided PERS. (6) Also relevant to the reviewer though not a named trigger: the retailer's „Klinisch erwiesen" / „Klinisch erwiesene wärmeschützende und feuchtigkeitsregulierende Wirkung" language names no study, sample size or methodology; per §3.3 EU claim legality means a dossier exists, never that an instrumental finished-product test exists, and it was treated as E0 throughout. (7) Not fired: the T7 `manufacturer_hold_level` trigger (the only hold statement is C3/C4 and is not a level), `candidate_below_tail` (no §7.10-qualifying route at any rank), the two-phase trigger (the architecture resolves to `emulsion` despite the shake instruction), the texture_fit row-4/row-5 trigger, and the T6 `repair_support_level` trigger.
